messages:
Ana: Hey all — quick Q. We're proposing a 30d retention for full request bodies but 7d for extracted sensitive snippets (emails/names). Need alignment on console UX, API header, and migration impact. cc @Mike :eyes:
Mike: Quick thought — 30d full for prod ok, but default dev orgs to 7d. Also: we'd want an explicit opt-in toggle for 'retain full bodies'.
Jamie: Strongly prefer not to persist raw PII at all. Can we store only derived metadata + irreversible hash?
Olivia: From compliance side, some regions want deletion rather than hashing. If hashing is used, it must be per-customer salted and documented.
devex: UX note — try to avoid technical jargon like 'PII' in the toggle. Label it 'sensitive data retention (emails, names, contact)'. Show a small modal explaining audit implications.
sre-bot: FYI deploybot scheduled maintenance at 2004001500 — any debug-mode logs will truncate bodies to 256 chars during deploy.
Mike: Proposed implementation: Console shows two toggles — 'retain full request bodies' and 'retain derived metadata'. API gets optional header X-RW-STORE-MODE: full|meta|none. Defaults: full=false, meta=true for new orgs.
Jamie: Example config snippet for the scrubber + retention we tested: ```yaml
request_logging:
  retention_days: 30
  pii_retention_days: 7
  pii_strategy: hash
  hash_algorithm: hmac-sha256
  hash_salt: per_customer_kms
  scrub_regex: "(?i)(?:email|ssn):\s*[^,]+"
```
Ana: Good. Two follow-ups: 1) update quotas/storage calc (30d bodies vs 7d meta) so billing reflects storage delta; 2) add an alert for accidental full-body retention flips during canary.
Olivia: Also require audit events for any toggle change: who changed it, when, and for which org. Those audit events need 7y retention per legal for some enterprise contracts.
devex: Rollout suggestion: canary 1% orgs -> 10% -> GA. Add banner in Console 'Beta retention controls' with link to docs and a clear rollback button.
Mike: I'll open a PR with the API header + migration plan and a quick script to backfill hashed metadata for existing logs. Any objections to the per-customer salted HMAC approach?
Jamie: No objections. Make sure salt is stored only in KMS and never in plaintext. Also add a test that scrubs across long prompts (multi-turn) so we don't accidentally leak earlier turns.
Ana: Can someone add a small perf eval for the scrubber (CPU/latency impact) and a verification that historic dashboards still function with metadata-only retention? @Jamie?
Jamie: On it — will run 500k synthetic requests through the scrubber and post perf numbers + false-positive/negative rates tomorrow. :rocket:
